newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Inquiry urged on Australia livestock exports.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Inquiry urged on Australia livestock exports.

text.p: The International Transport Workers' Federation (ITF) has called for a full inquiry into the export of livestock from Australia following the loss of 1,592 head of cattle on a vessel which sunk off Guam on Sunday.
The Dutch-owned Philippine-registered vessel Guernsey Express sank on route to Japan during bad weather.
"This sort of tragedy cannot be allowed to continue," ITF Australia co-ordinator Trevor Charles said in a statement.
This September the Panamanian flag vessel Uniceb was gutted by fire on route to Jordan. One crewman and 67,000 Australian sheep died in the inferno, Charles said.

The inquiry should include an examination of the suitability of vessels currently being used, training, wages and conditions of seafarers engaged in the trade and conditions and welfare of livestock during the voyage, he said.
"The current trend, if allowed to continue unabated, has the capacity to do great harm to our international reputation and a trade worth A$316 million last year," he said.
The sinking of the Guernsey Express showed that the Uniceb disaster was not a freak accident but a sign of something terribly wrong in the trade, he said.
